## Course Information

### 0401341 Islamic Movements  (3 Credit Hours)
This course reviews the reasons behind the rise of Islamic movements, especially colonialism, the downfall of the Islamic caliphate, cultural invasion, and touches on the most famous Islamic movements in India and Pakistan and the contemporary Salafi trends.

---

### 0401440 Certification of Qur'an Recitation  (1 hr. theory and 4 hrs. practical) (3 Credit Hours)
This course will help students to read the whole Qur’an to their teachers according to one Qur’anic reading or more and then to get a certificate in reciting the Qur’an.

---

### 0401441 Oratory in Mosques  (1 hr. theory and 4 hrs. practical) (3 Credit Hours)
The goal of this course is to qualify a student to be able to deliver a Jum’ah speech properly. It teaches students oratory skills, good speech, and successful preaching. Students will be trained to deliver Jum’ah speeches during the term and will give at least 10 Jum’ah speeches under the supervision of their teachers.

---

### 0401442 Da’wah Media  (3 Credit Hours)
This course is about media in terms of its importance, objectives, history, development, elements, properties, methods, tools, and effects. It focuses on the properties of the Islamic media, conditions, ethics, the appropriate tools and methods, and the necessity of making full use of this effective weapon in shaping public opinion.

---

### 0431222 Analytic Hadith  (3 Credit Hours)
This course aims to discuss certain accounts of the Prophet from different aspects such as their meanings, ascriptions (chain), and words from the following books:

- **Sahih al-Bukhari with Fath al-Bari**, 15 accounts from the following chapters: 
  - (Bad’ al-Wahy, al-‘Ilm, al-‘Umrah and Khabar al-‘Ahad).
  
- **Sahih Muslim with Sharh al-Nawawi**, 15 accounts from the following chapters: 
  - (al-Iman, al-Jihad wa al-Imarah, al-Libas wa al-Zinah and Sifat al-Munafiqin).

- **Al-Sunan al-Arba'ah and Musnad al-Imam Ahmad**, 20 selected accounts.

All this in addition to other positions to be read by the student himself from various resources.
